title: feature: CPU Core

description: Create a CPU Core that implements the CPU diagram.
steps:
Create core.h and core.c--two files implementing the CPU diagram.
It should contain all of the major components of the CPU like GPR (16), SPRs like PC and IR, ALU, control bits, bus address, bus return, etc.
Feel free to use global variables, structs, unions, etc.

title: docs: ISA Validation and Disassembly
label: feature
description: Explore the isa.c and isa.h files by implementing the `isa_is_valid` and `isa_disassemble` functions.
steps:
Remember to include good documentation on their purposes.
`bool isa_is_valid(uint8_t opcode)` takes an opcode as we've defined in isa.md and returns whether it's a real opcode or not. This can probably be done with testing particular bits, and brute force would be a large if statement. For example, 11111111 is not a valid opcode, doesn't match the table at all.
`void isa_disassemble(uint32_t word, char* buf, size_t buflen)` is definitely trickier, takes an opcode, and CREATES an assembly-like instruction. For example, `0b0020001 1100 XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXXXXXX` should fill the buffer with `POP R12`. This will be useful for confirming if our example code is compiled correctly.

If this is easier to code in python, I would recommend doing that first and then asing an LLM to make C code out of it or other creative ideas.
NOTE: consider moving to m2 if unfeasible during m1.
